prompt: You have a discovery call tomorrow with a founder who filled in your website form. Order your preparation steps, first first.

task.prompt: You have a discovery call tomorrow with a founder who filled in your website form. Order your preparation steps, first first.

items.label: Write 3-5 discovery questions specific to their situation
Pick one or two relevant case studies to mention if they fit
Send a short agenda and confirm the time and meeting link
Re-read the form submission and any earlier emails
Research the company and the founder (website, LinkedIn, recent news)

task.explanation: Start from what they told you, add context, plan questions, prepare proof, then confirm logistics with the client.

prompt: Mark the problems in this meeting confirmation email.

task.prompt: Mark the problems in this meeting confirmation email.

segments.text: Hi Leila, looking forward to our call.

segments.issue: No time zone; with international clients this causes missed calls.
The meeting link should be in the confirmation and calendar invite now.

segments.text: Agenda: your goals for the marketplace app, current blockers, and next steps (30 minutes).
If anyone else from your team should join, feel free to forward this.

prompt: You use Calendly to let inbound leads book discovery calls.

task.prompt: You use Calendly to let inbound leads book discovery calls.

steps.question: Which booking form setup is best?
options: Name, email, company and one optional question: 'What would you like to build?'
Fifteen required fields including budget, tech stack and full requirements
Only a first name
No form, just a time slot
steps.explanation: A short form gives you enough to prepare without scaring people away from booking.

steps.question: A lead books for tomorrow from another country. What should you check?
options: That they have a budget over a set amount
Nothing, the tool handles everything
That the time shows correctly in both time zones and the video link is in the invite
That they have signed an NDA
steps.explanation: Time zone and link issues are the most common causes of no-shows; confirm both.

steps.question: How can you reduce no-shows?
options: Send a short reminder the day before with the agenda and link
Call them hourly on the day
Book them twice in case they forget
Avoid reminders so you do not annoy them
steps.explanation: A brief, useful reminder is the standard way to cut no-shows.

prompt: Rank these meeting agendas for a 30-minute first call with a prospect, best first.

task.prompt: Rank these meeting agendas for a 30-minute first call with a prospect, best first.

items.label: Full demo of five past projects (30 min)
Their goals and current situation (10 min), challenges (10 min), how we might help and next steps (10 min)
Our company introduction (20 min), their questions (10 min)

task.explanation: A first call should centre on the prospect. Long intros, unstructured chats and back-to-back demos leave no time to learn their needs.

prompt: Mark the weak items in this pre-call research note.

task.prompt: Mark the weak items in this pre-call research note.

segments.text: Company: GreenCart, online grocery delivery in two cities, about 40 staff.
Contact: Maria, co-founder and COO, ex-logistics manager.
Recent news: raised a seed round two months ago.
Need: probably wants everything, will figure out on the call.
segments.issue: No hypothesis; research should suggest what they likely need, e.g. a driver or customer app.
Asks for facts the research already answers; it wastes call time and looks unprepared.

segments.text: Relevant proof: our delivery-tracking app for a courier client.

prompt: Why send a short agenda before a sales call?

options: It replaces the need to prepare
It is a legal requirement
It guarantees the deal
It sets expectations and lets the prospect add what matters to them
mcq.explanation: An agenda shows respect for their time and lets them shape the call, which improves attendance and focus.

prompt: A prospect books a call and you have 10 minutes to prepare. What is the most useful thing to do?

options: Rehearse your company pitch
Prepare a price quote
Draft the contract
Read what they submitted and check their website and LinkedIn quickly
mcq.explanation: Knowing who they are and what they asked for lets you ask good questions; quotes and contracts come later.

prompt: What should the calendar invite for a client call always include?

options: Your full company brochure
Your pricing table
Only the date
Date, time with time zone, video link and a one-line purpose
mcq.explanation: Those details prevent confusion and no-shows; sales material does not belong in the invite.
